articles.title: The autistic brain processes faces differently than scientists thought
articles.summary: A major new study reveals that autistic children’s brains process faces differently, and those differences may begin earlier than scientists previously thought. Researchers found that brain signals associated with recognizing faces become more specialized as neurotypical children grow older, but show much less change in autistic children. The discovery could help explain why some autistic people have difficulty…

articles.title: Could tomato paste help your brain? A three-month trial points to modest gains in attention and memory
articles.summary: Tomatoes are the main dietary source of lycopene, a red pigment that can reach the brain. In a new trial, daily tomato paste was linked to better attention and memory scores, along with preliminary changes in how certain brain networks communicate.

articles.title: Household chaos does not directly cause poor grades, twin study suggests
articles.summary: A disorganized home is often linked to poor academic performance, but a large twin study reveals that shared genetics and broader family environments are to blame, not the noise and clutter itself.

articles.title: Autistic children’s brains respond less to the emotional meaning of sentences, fMRI study finds
articles.summary: When children hear a sentence about someone’s feelings, part of the brain’s language system typically responds more strongly than it does to a sentence about objects. In autistic children, that difference was smaller.

articles.title: News coverage of psilocybin often outpaces the science, systematic review finds
articles.summary: Researchers compared 70 psilocybin trial publications with 172 news articles. Both reported positive results at similar rates, but news coverage tended to present the benefits as established and rarely discussed the small, early-stage nature of the research.

articles.title: Just a few minutes of speech may offer a window into brain health and aging
articles.summary: Researchers trained a machine learning model to estimate a person’s age from short voice recordings. In a study of nearly 3,000 adults across Latin America, speech in people with dementia tended to sound older than in cognitively healthy adults.

articles.title: Glutamate receptors may help explain the brain structure behind children’s math and reading abilities
articles.summary: Of 19 chemical signaling systems examined, only one consistently matched the brain structure linked to children’s math and reading abilities across two independent groups: NMDA receptors, which respond to the neurotransmitter glutamate.

Now, scientists have identified a mushroom species, Lanmaoa asiatica, responsible for these extraordinary hallucinations in China and the Philippines.

articles.title: Mediterranean diet may boost tiny proteins that protect the heart and brain

articles.title: Breakthrough PTSD treatment achieves 68% remission rate in clinical trial
articles.summary: A newly FDA-cleared PTSD treatment uses personalized brain mapping and magnetic stimulation to target abnormal brain activity, with a clinical trial reporting a 52% reduction in symptoms and 68% remission. Researchers believe the technology could transform PTSD care and pave the way for more precise treatments for other mental health conditions.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden messaging system deep inside the brain
articles.summary: A tiny region deep within the brain has surprised scientists by revealing a remarkably sophisticated communication system. Previously thought to broadcast the same chemical signal throughout the brain, this region actually sends targeted messages that help control learning, attention, and behavior, according to new research in mice.

articles.title: Millions take fish oil for brain health. A two-year study found no benefit
articles.summary: A surprising two-year clinical trial found that fish oil supplements successfully delivered omega-3s to the brain but failed to improve memory or protect against Alzheimer's-related brain shrinkage. Researchers suspect that getting these nutrients through a healthy diet may offer benefits that supplements alone cannot provide.

articles.title: A simple daily fiber supplement reduced arthritis pain and improved strength
articles.summary: A new clinical trial suggests that a simple daily fiber supplement could significantly reduce knee osteoarthritis pain, improve muscle strength, and make the body less sensitive to pain. Researchers discovered that the benefits may be linked to changes in gut bacteria and the hormone GLP-1, revealing a promising new approach to arthritis relief.

articles.title: Noninvasive focused ultrasound treatment can ease motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease

His hands shook so badly that he struggled to hold utensils and couldn't sign his name. He stopped playing pickleball—a sport he once enjoyed—despite taking a widely prescribed medication for managing motor symptoms, such as rigidity or stiffness, slow movement, involuntary muscle movement (dyskinesia) and tremors.

articles.title: Workplace ergonomics may do little to ease arm, neck or shoulder pain
articles.summary: An updated Cochrane review has found that ergonomic interventions show no meaningful benefit for pain, function, recovery or sick leave in workers with work-related complaints of the arm, neck or shoulder (CANS), compared with no treatment.

articles.title: Scientists discover the immune system’s hidden sense of touch
articles.summary: Scientists at McGill University have discovered a surprising new ability of immune cells that could change how we understand long-term immunity. Researchers found that T cells can actually sense how stiff their surrounding tissues are, using these physical signals to help determine whether they develop into long-lasting memory cells that protect against future infections.

articles.title: Low testosterone may make sugar far more harmful to your liver

articles.title: Scientists discover a surprising clue to why some brains resist Alzheimer’s
articles.summary: Why do some people stay mentally sharp even when their brains show signs of Alzheimer’s disease? Scientists in the Netherlands may have uncovered an important clue hidden in a rare group of immature brain cells. Researchers discovered that these cells remain present even in people over 80, but their behavior differs dramatically between those who develop dementia and those who remain cognitively healthy.

articles.title: Just two drinks a day may be far riskier than you think
articles.summary: A major new study reveals that drinking just two alcoholic beverages a day is associated with a 1 in 25 lifetime risk of death from alcohol-related causes, challenging the idea that moderate drinking is harmless. Researchers also found no significant overall health benefits from alcohol, with risks rising as consumption increases.

articles.title: Low-dose aspirin linked to 70% lower dementia risk, but there's a catch
articles.summary: A common, inexpensive medication could hold an unexpected clue to preventing dementia. Researchers found that older adults with a specific genetic profile had a 70% lower relative risk of dementia when taking low-dose aspirin, even though previous studies found no overall protective effect. The discovery suggests that genetics could help explain why some people benefit while others do not.

articles.title: Popular cannabis sleep gummies may have a hidden dark side
articles.summary: A cannabis-derived ingredient commonly found in sleep gummies may be more habit-forming than previously thought, with new research showing that repeated exposure caused tolerance and withdrawal symptoms in mice. Scientists warn that CBN may carry risks similar to THC, although its long-term effects in humans remain largely unknown.
